- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid overcorrecting; maintain slight upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward moves), model should not overreact to recent spikes; apply mild lag correction.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.3 within 3 days), adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal by smoothing out abrupt directional changes.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates prices after a strong upward move (e.g., +10%+ above true), apply a downward bias of 3–5% for the next 5–7 days to reflect market cooling.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), forecast should be anchored to recent 7–14 day average, not extreme highs/lows.
